summary.value: Arizona licenses construction contractors at state level only, and forbids the local layer in terms: cities — including charter cities — towns and counties may not require a licence of a contractor the state has licensed.
summary.evidence: Cities, including charter cities, towns and counties shall not require licenses of any construction contractors licensed by statute

jurisdiction_model.local_layer_note: Arizona is the opposite of Ohio and Georgia on this point and it is worth the customer's attention: A.R.S. § 32-1101.01 pre-empts municipal and county contractor licensing outright. The pre-emption is of LICENSING. It does not touch permits, inspections, transaction privilege (sales) tax licences or business registrations, which Arizona municipalities do operate, and no such requirement is modelled here.

who_must_hold.value: Any person, firm, partnership, corporation, association or other organisation acting as, offering to act as, bidding as or purporting to have the capacity of a contractor in Arizona must hold a licence in good standing in its own name.
who_must_hold.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1151 Engaging in contracting without license prohibited
who_must_hold.evidence: It is unlawful for any person, firm, partnership, corporation, association or other organization
who_must_hold.note: Securing a permit from a government agency, or employing a person on a construction project, is prima facie evidence in an Arizona court that a contract exists — so pulling a permit is itself evidence of contracting.

scope_note.value: Arizona's statutory category. The Registrar subdivides it into trade classifications and the air conditioning, heating and refrigeration trade's classification codes are commonly written C-39 / K-39 / CR-39, but the classification list is published in the Registrar's rules, not in statute.
scope_note.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1102 Classification of licenses; contracting business
scope_note.evidence: Specialty residential contracting, which is engaging in the residential contracting business by the performance of construction work requiring special skill
scope_note.note: The category and its statutory definition are verified at A.R.S. § 32-1102. The trade classification CODES are not: they live in the Arizona Administrative Code title 4 chapter 9 and on the Registrar's classification table, neither of which could be fetched (see coverage notes). They are named here only so a reader recognises the licence in hand, and no requirement in this record is attached to a code.

expiry_rule.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1123.01 Staggered periods of licensure; biennial renewal
expiry_rule.evidence: The registrar shall maintain a system of staggered licensure to distribute the work of licensure throughout the twelve months of the year.
expiry_rule.note: Staggered, not common: the Registrar spreads renewal dates across all twelve months, so the date comes from the licence, never from a calendar. grace_period.value: None. The licence is suspended by operation of law on the next business day following its renewal date. It can be reactivated within one year of that suspension by filing the application, paying the renewal fee and adding $50; after one year a new application and a new licence are required.
grace_period.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1125 Renewal of license; qualifying party
grace_period.evidence: a license issued under this chapter is suspended on the next business day following its renewal date by operation of law
grace_period.note: A renewal application posted or received on or before the renewal date, with a valid bond on file, lets the contractor keep operating until the renewal licence is actually issued — so the postmark, not the issue date, is what protects an Arizona contractor. Derived from statute; the Registrar's own guidance could not be read.

late_fee.evidence: The penalty for failure to apply for renewal of a license within the time prescribed by this chapter is $50.

licence_types.name: Specialty Dual Licensed Contractor — air conditioning, heating and refrigeration trade classification

who_must_hold.value: Any person, firm, partnership, corporation, association or other organisation acting as, offering to act as, bidding as or purporting to have the capacity of a contractor in Arizona must hold a licence in good standing in its own name.
who_must_hold.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1151 Engaging in contracting without license prohibited
who_must_hold.evidence: It is unlawful for any person, firm, partnership, corporation, association or other organization
who_must_hold.note: Securing a permit from a government agency, or employing a person on a construction project, is prima facie evidence in an Arizona court that a contract exists — so pulling a permit is itself evidence of contracting.

scope_note.value: Arizona's statutory category. The Registrar subdivides it into trade classifications and the air conditioning, heating and refrigeration trade's classification codes are commonly written C-39 / K-39 / CR-39, but the classification list is published in the Registrar's rules, not in statute.
scope_note.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1102 Classification of licenses; contracting business
scope_note.evidence: Specialty dual licensed contracting, which is engaging in the contracting business in the performance of construction work requiring special skill
scope_note.note: The category and its statutory definition are verified at A.R.S. § 32-1102. The trade classification CODES are not: they live in the Arizona Administrative Code title 4 chapter 9 and on the Registrar's classification table, neither of which could be fetched (see coverage notes). They are named here only so a reader recognises the licence in hand, and no requirement in this record is attached to a code.

requirement.value: The qualifying party must have four years' practical or management trade experience dealing specifically with the type of construction applied for, at least two of those years within the last ten.
requirement.evidence: Have a minimum of four years' practical or management trade experience, at least two of which must have been within the last ten years

alternatives.value: Technical training at an accredited college or university, or in a manufacturer's accredited training programme, may substitute for up to two of the four years. expiry_rule.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1123.01 Staggered periods of licensure; biennial renewal
expiry_rule.evidence: The registrar shall maintain a system of staggered licensure to distribute the work of licensure throughout the twelve months of the year.
expiry_rule.note: Staggered, not common: the Registrar spreads renewal dates across all twelve months, so the date comes from the licence, never from a calendar. With the biennial cycle above this is issue date + 24 months. Derived from statute; the Registrar does not restate it anywhere this pass could read.

grace_period.value: None. The licence is suspended by operation of law on the next business day following its renewal date. It can be reactivated within one year of that suspension by filing the application, paying the renewal fee and adding $50; after one year a new application and a new licence are required.
grace_period.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1125 Renewal of license; qualifying party
grace_period.evidence: a license issued under this chapter is suspended on the next business day following its renewal date by operation of law
grace_period.note: A renewal application posted or received on or before the renewal date, with a valid bond on file, lets the contractor keep operating until the renewal licence is actually issued — so the postmark, not the issue date, is what protects an Arizona contractor. Derived from statute; the Registrar's own guidance could not be read.

late_fee.evidence: The penalty for failure to apply for renewal of a license within the time prescribed by this chapter is $50.
late_fee.note: The one Arizona money figure in this record that is a PRICE rather than a ceiling: the statute says the penalty 'is $50', not 'not more than $50'. Confidence is low only because the source is statute and the Registrar does not restate it.

required.evidence: Before granting an original contractor's license, the registrar shall require of the applicant a surety bond in a form acceptable to the registrar
required.note: Arizona is the FIRST state in this knowledge base with a bond requirement established at all — the other eighteen records carry bond.required as unknown. And it bites twice: no licence may be RENEWED unless the bond or cash deposit is in full force and effect, so a lapsed bond is a lapsed licence. Confidence is low because the source is statute and the Registrar's own page could not be read.

amount.note: NOT A SINGLE NUMBER, by design. A.R.S. § 32-1152(B) has the Registrar fix the amount within statutory bands 'after giving due consideration to the volume of work and the classification contemplated by the applicant'. For a Specialty Dual Licensed Contractor the band is a single bond carrying an amount for each classification — the commercial half by volume band, the residential half between $1,000 and $7,500. The applicant's own estimated annual volume selects the band, so no figure can be printed for a contractor until that estimate exists. The Registrar of Contractors publishes this figure; the Registrar's site could not be read. alternative.value: A cash deposit with the State Treasurer, in the amount of the bond, may be posted instead of a surety bond. Where there are no outstanding claims it can be withdrawn two years after the licence ends.
alternative.evidence: The surety bonds shall be executed by the contractor as principal with a corporation duly authorized to transact surety business in this state.
alternative.note: The cash-deposit alternative and the two-year withdrawal rule are in the same subsection as the quoted sentence, A.R.S. § 32-1152(D). A residential or dual licensee must ALSO either post a further $200,000 bond for actual damages under § 32-1132 or join the residential contractors' recovery fund and pay an assessment of not more than $600 per biennial period.

qualifying_individual_rule.value: Each licence names a qualifying party. That person may not take other employment conflicting with the duty to supervise the licensee's work, and may qualify ONE additional licensee only where there is at least 25% common ownership of both entities, or one is a 25%-owned subsidiary of the other.
qualifying_individual_rule.evidence: Such person may act in the capacity of the qualifying party for one additional licensee
qualifying_individual_rule.note: This is the field that decides whether a roll-up can staff an Arizona acquisition with the qualifier it already has: two licences per person, and only inside a 25% common-ownership group. The qualifying party is also responsible for the licensee's violations for regulatory purposes, though § 32-1127(B) says that imposes no personal liability.

entity_registration.value: A corporate or LLC applicant must attest that it is in good standing with the Arizona Corporation Commission, and must name every officer, director, manager or member and every owner of 25% or more of the stock or beneficial interest.
entity_registration.evidence: The name and address of the qualifying party.

change_notification_deadline.value: 15 days to notify the Registrar in writing, in a duty falling on BOTH the licensee and the departing qualifying party, and 60 days to requalify through another person. Miss the 60 days and the licence is suspended automatically, by operation of law, until a new qualifying party is in place.
change_notification_deadline.source_title: A.R.S. § 32-1127.01 Qualifying parties; disassociation with license; requalification
change_notification_deadline.evidence: both the licensee and the qualifying party shall notify the registrar in writing within fifteen days after the disassociation
change_notification_deadline.note: The tightest qualifier deadline in the knowledge base: Arizona 15 days to notify and 60 to requalify, against Ohio's 90-day reassignment wait and Texas's 30 business days. Separately, A.R.S. § 32-1122(B)(4) requires notice of ANY change to the information on the application within 30 days. This is an event-triggered deadline, not a date on a licence.

Consequently the ACTUAL FEES ARE NOT IN THIS RECORD. The statute sets ceilings ('not more than $350', 'not more than $1,000') and the Registrar sets the price inside them. Application fee and renewal fee are therefore empty. The only money figures recorded are the $50 late penalty and the bond bands, both of which the statute states as amounts rather than as maxima.

The ROC trade classification codes (C-39 / K-39 / CR-39 for this trade) are named in the scope note for recognition only. The classification list is in the Arizona Administrative Code title 4 chapter 9 and on the Registrar's own table, neither of which could be fetched, so no requirement in this record is attached to a code and the three licence types are the statutory categories rather than the Registrar's classifications.

Continuing education is NOT ESTABLISHED for Arizona, in either direction. The statute imposes none; the Registrar has rulemaking power under § 32-1105 and its rules could not be read. The record says 'not established', which is the honest answer, and not 'no CE required', which would be a guess a customer could act on.
Reciprocity is not established. A.R.S. § 32-1125 points at chapter 43 (§ 32-4301, universal licensure) which was not fetched, and the Registrar's reciprocity page is blocked.

The residential contractors' recovery fund (A.R.S. §§ 32-1131 to 32-1140) affects residential and dual licensees and is summarised in the bond alternative note; it is not modelled as a trackable obligation with its own deadline.
